we have identified Xmc as a novel Xctr1‐targeted effector of FGF signaling in Xenopus laevismorphogenesis.

1) we have identified a novel FGF‐responsive gene, Xmc, that is expressed in the notochord following the loss of maternal Xctr1; 2) Xctr1 is not required for Xmc expression in animal cap explants; and 3) loss of Xmc function inhibits the elongation of FGC‐treated animal caps following Xctr1 loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of morphogenesis in the developing Xenopus embryo.
the role of the Xenopus CTR1 protein, Xctr1, in FGF‐mediated signaling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Xctr1‐dependent mesoderm formation is required for FGF‐mediated elongational morphogenesis, and Xmc is a key effector for Xctr1‐ independent morphogenesis.
